title: Runway Oscillation Mitigation and Capacity Bucketizer
content:
Purpose:
Short working sheet to capture a pragmatic allocator ("bucketizer") for reserved GPU commits that reduces utilization oscillation and improves runway predictability. Target audience: product ops + finance + sales when structuring renewals, plus SRE for pool sizing guidance.

Summary / quick takeaways:
- Problem: large committed pools exhibit utilization oscillation (time-of-day, campaign-driven spikes, onboarding waves) that causes high peak-to-average ratios and wasted reserved time.
- Proposal: slice reserved commits into 3–5 buckets by functional cadence and commit term (steady-run bucket, seasonal bucket, growth buffer). Combine with a prioritized backfill / spot-offset policy.
- Expected impact: 6–13% reduction in effective idle for typical mixed customers; 10–20% improved runway against churn in 6–12 month horizon for pilot customers.

Key definitions and variables (single-sheet calculator style):
- CommitSize = committed GPUs (units)
- AveLoad = average in-use GPUs across measurement window (90d)
- PeakLoad = 95th percentile usage (90d)
- UtilRate = AveLoad / CommitSize
- OscAmplitude = (PeakLoad - AveLoad) / AveLoad -> describes oscillation magnitude
- BucketCount = number of reserved bands (3 recommended)
- BucketTerms = [12m, 6m, 3m] (term lengths)
- BufferPct = fraction of commit maintained as short-term buffer (default 8%)

Simple allocator logic (prototype rules):
1) Steady-run bucket (B1): match long-running baseline = round(AveLoad * 1.05) -> term 12m (high discount).
2) Seasonal bucket (B2): cover predictable amplitude = round((PeakLoad - AveLoad) * 0.6) -> term 6m (moderate discount).
3) Growth/buffer bucket (B3): cover erratic onboarding spikes and runway hedging = max(round(CommitSize * BufferPct), min_unit) -> term 3m (low discount).
4) If predicted shortfall in B2/B3 coincides with excess in other regions, route overflow to cheaper spot/preemptable lanes and apply credit offsets.

Example scenario table (row format: ScenarioName | CommitSize | AveLoad | PeakLoad | UtilRate | OscAmp | Bucket allocation B1/B2/B3 | Estimated idle %)
- steady-flat | 200 | 180 | 190 | 0.90 | 0.056 | B1=189,B2=6,B3=5 | idle~5%
- seasonal-wave | 200 | 130 | 200 | 0.65 | 0.538 | B1=137,B2=42,B3=21 | idle~14% -> expected cut to ~8%
- onboarding-spike | 200 | 120 | 220 | 0.60 | 0.833 | B1=126,B2=54,B3=20 | idle~25% -> cut to ~15% with buffer/offset

Cost wiring and illustrative math (for finance):
- Assumptions: list price per GPU-month = $X (sensitive parameter), committed discount bands: 12m=60% off list, 6m=45% off list, 3m=20% off list, spot effective price = 15% of list when available.
- Effective blended rate = (sum_{buckets} bucket_size * bucket_price) / CommitSize
- Marginal cost saved by bucketizer = baseline_blended_rate - new_blended_rate -> convert to monthly $ and runway months = committed_balance / monthly_savings.

Heuristic rules for sales packaging (talking points):
- Offer baseline (B1) as the high-discount anchor that covers 70–85% of typical steady-state usage.
- Offer seasonal add-ons (B2) as 6-month top-ups priced to reflect mid-term utilization; allow rollover credits for unused seasonal capacity (soft credits) to reduce buyer risk.
- Offer short-term growth buffers (B3) as 3-month auto-renewing credits with explicit backfill policy and option to convert to B2 on renewal.
- Include explicit off-peak migration option for customers willing to shift non-latency workloads to lower-cost times (gives us additional utilization headroom).

Sensitivity checks to run (sheet tabs / quick rows):
- Discount sensitivity: vary 12m/6m/3m discounts ±10pp and compute blended rate impact.
- Oscillation sensitivity: sweep OscAmplitude 0.1->1.2 and record idle reduction.
- Churn shock: simulate 20% reduction in AveLoad over 3 months and test runway extension with bucketized commits vs monolithic commit.
- Region mismatch: test scenario where 20% of traffic migrates between regions -> measure cross-region buffer requirement.

Open questions & TODOs:
- What is the right minimum unit (min_unit) for bucket sizing? (engineering constraint: GPUs are allocated in whole machines; often min_unit=8 for A100 pods). Follow up with infra for concrete VM shapes. @Ava to confirm.
- Policy for unused seasonal capacity: should we automatically convert to credits or return to pool? Input needed from finance on revenue recognition (CC / deferrals). JIRA-DED-891 tracks revenue treatment.
- SRE: how to implement automated routing for overflow -> ticket to infra team for proto (link above).

Quick simulation outputs (notes from initial run):
- Pilot customer A (SaaS search, heavy daytime peaks): baseline idle 19% -> bucketizer reduces to 11% -> monthly savings ~$8.4k (per 200-GPU commit assumptions).
- Pilot customer B (ML infra, steady but growing): small net change in immediate idle but improves 12-month runway by ~1.2 months.

Risks / failure modes:
- Over-fragmentation: too many small buckets increases ops complexity and friction in sales negotiations. Keep bucket count <=5.
- Mispriced short-term buffers could cannibalize long-term bookings. Pricing guardrails required.
- Behavioral: customers may game seasonal buckets — require clear policies for rollover and conversion.

Next steps (concrete):
- [ ] Finalize min_unit constraints with infra (owner: Ava, due: 2026-03-01).
- [ ] Run 90d cohort simulation across top 30 committed customers (owner: Priya, due: 2026-02-28).
- [ ] Draft sales playbook language and packaging examples (owner: Liam, due: 2026-03-10).
- [ ] Create an internal pricing calculator sheet (tabbed) and attach to this doc for finance review.
